articles.title: Pressure on landlord costs increase as Renters’ Rights Act looms
articles.summary: The average landlord is now carrying £714,000 in borrowing and paying around £25,000 a year in interest alone, before tax, maintenance or compliance costs are taken into account, according to new analysis from Pepper Money and Pegasus Insights.
articles.ai_summary:
- Average landlords in the UK are burdened with £714,000 in borrowing and face annual interest payments of £25,000, highlighting significant financial pressure ahead of impending regulatory changes.  
- The looming Renters’ Rights Act is set to intensify cost challenges for landlords, adding to their existing financial obligations of tax, maintenance, and compliance.

articles.title: Wave of last-minute instructions as landlords exit ahead of RRA
articles.summary: With the Renters’ Rights Act coming into force this Friday, Kent and London law firm Thackray Williams says it has had a wave of last-minute instructions from landlords looking to exit the market.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords rush to leave the market as the Renters' Rights Act takes effect this Friday, prompting a surge in last-minute instructions to law firms.  
- Kent and London’s Thackray Williams reports a significant increase in requests from landlords seeking to exit ahead of the new legislation.

articles.title: Chief property ombudsman welcomes RRA but says landlords need support
articles.summary: The UK’s chief property ombudsman Lesley Horton has said she welcomes the reforms coming with the Renters’ Right Act implementation this week but says that small-scale landlords in particular will need support to adapt to the changes.
articles.ai_summary:
- Chief Property Ombudsman Lesley Horton endorses the upcoming Renters' Right Act reforms, emphasizing their positive impact on the rental market.
- Horton highlights the urgent need for support for small-scale landlords to ensure they can effectively navigate the new regulations.

articles.title: Nervous landlords prompt tenfold rise in instructions, says agent
articles.summary: North-east residential lettings agency Xenia Lettings says it has seen a tenfold rise in instructions from property owners since the start of 2026 as private landlords seek expert help to navigate the Renters’ Rights Act, the biggest phase of which goes live on Friday.
articles.ai_summary:
- Xenia Lettings reports a tenfold increase in instructions from landlords in early 2026, driven by uncertainty surrounding the new Renters' Rights Act.  
- Private property owners are actively seeking expert guidance to effectively manage the significant changes coming into effect.

articles.title: Reeves reported to be considering rent controls
articles.summary: Chancellor Rachel Reeves is reported to be thinking about imposing rent controls on Private Rented Sector landlords as part of a range of measures to limit the impact of the Iran War on household finances.
articles.ai_summary:
- Chancellor Rachel Reeves is contemplating rent controls for Private Rented Sector landlords to mitigate the financial impact of the Iran War on households.  
- The proposed measures aim to address rising living costs and enhance affordability in the rental market.

articles.title: HMRC increases scrutiny of residential valuations
articles.summary: HMRC is increasingly challenging residential property valuations in inheritance tax (IHT) returns, with the number of cases referred to the Valuation Office Agency (VOA) rising 23.5% in the last year, according to research from TWM Solicitors, a private wealth and family law firm.
articles.ai_summary:
- HMRC is stepping up scrutiny of residential property valuations, leading to a 23.5% increase in cases sent to the Valuation Office Agency for review in the past year.  
- This trend highlights growing challenges for homeowners regarding inheritance tax (IHT) returns and the accuracy of property valuations.

articles.title: Landlords urged to carry out more detailed pre-purchase checks after RRA

articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are advised to conduct thorough pre-purchase checks on rental properties to safeguard their investments following the Renters’ Rights Act implementation on May 1.  
- The new legislation emphasizes the need for enhanced due diligence to navigate potential liabilities and challenges in the rental market.

articles.title: Most landlords to be stricter choosing tenants – survey

articles.ai_summary:
- A quarter of landlords are considering leaving the market due to the new Renters’ Rights Act.  
- Among those staying, 60% plan to implement stricter tenant vetting processes.

articles.title: Maintenance expert shares top Spring tips to cut costs

articles.ai_summary:
- Spring is the ideal time for landlords to address winter-related maintenance issues and comply with new responsibilities under the Renters’ Rights Act.  
- Proactive maintenance can help cut costs and enhance property management effectiveness.

articles.title: Pressure on rents to continue despite halving house price growth forecast
articles.summary: Knight Frank has halved its near-term house price growth forecast to 1.5% for 2026 and lowered itsrental forecasts marginally, due to the economic impacts of conflict in the Middle East.
articles.ai_summary:
- Knight Frank has reduced its house price growth forecast to 1.5% for 2026 amid economic uncertainty from the Middle East conflict.  
- Despite a slight decrease in rental forecasts, pressure on rents is expected to persist.

articles.title: Four in five landlords unprepared for Renters’ Right Act
articles.summary: Four in five landlords (82%) are concerned about the impact of the Renters’ Rights Act, with one in two (44%) very concerned. Meanwhile, three-quarters (75%) of landlords say regulation has made them less likely to grow their portfolios, and half (49%) are planning to sell or reduce their stake within two months.
articles.ai_summary:
- **Landlord Alarm**: 82% of landlords are worried about the upcoming Renters’ Rights Act, with nearly half (44%) feeling very concerned about its potential impact.
- **Portfolio Pessimism**: 75% of landlords feel that regulations deter portfolio growth, and 49% are considering selling or scaling back their investments in the next two months.

articles.title: Energy efficiency and EPC ratings become higher focus for tenants
articles.summary: Landlords must consider how to improve EPC ratings to attract tenants, even ahead of the new requirement to upgrade rental properties to a C rating by 2030. It comes as energy efficiency of properties has gained even greater focus as tenants look to save money after the energy price hikes caused by the Iran War.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords need to enhance EPC ratings to attract tenants, with a 2030 deadline to upgrade rental properties to a C rating looming.  
- Rising energy costs due to the Iran War have intensified tenants' demand for energy-efficient homes.

articles.ai_summary:

- Industry outlook remains bleak, highlighting a lack of confidence in governmental changes to planning policies.

articles.title: Landlords warned a hidden leak could cost thousands
articles.summary: With more than half (58%) of hidden leaks originating outside a property, landlords must remember to focus on the maintenance of pipework outside as well as inside the property, leak detection specialist Aspect has warned.
articles.ai_summary:
- Over 58% of hidden leaks occur outside properties, highlighting the importance of regular maintenance on external pipework for landlords.
- Failing to address outdoor plumbing can lead to costly repairs, as emphasized by leak detection expert Aspect.

articles.title: As RRA deadline looms, 5 top tips for landlords
articles.summary: From 1 May 2026, the Renters’ Rights Act will implement some of the biggest changes to the Private Rented Sector in England and Wales. The Act will aim to balance landlord and tenant rights and will impose new requirements and regulatory oversight on landlords.
articles.ai_summary:
- The Renters’ Rights Act, effective from 1 May 2026, will introduce significant reforms to the Private Rented Sector, enhancing tenant protections while adjusting landlord obligations.  
- Landlords must prepare for new regulations and compliance requirements as the Act seeks to create a more equitable rental market in England and Wales.

articles.title: 84% of landlords not ready for RRA – survey
articles.summary: More than eight in ten (84%) of landlords are unprepared for the Renters’ Rights Act go-live on May 1, with 58% at high risk of non-compliance according to new figures.
articles.ai_summary:
- **Majority Unprepared:** A staggering 84% of landlords are not ready for the Renters’ Rights Act implementation on May 1.  
- **High Compliance Risk:** 58% of landlords face a significant risk of non-compliance with the new regulations.

articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are shifting focus from expansion to restructuring their portfolios and financing to adapt to changing rental demand amid slowing rental growth, as highlighted by the ONS.
- The recent slowdown in rental growth signals a critical need for landlords to optimize their investments rather than simply grow their portfolios.
